title: Conformal selective prediction with cost aware deferral for safe clinical triage under distribution shift
research_question: Can calibrated probabilities, conformal prediction, and cost-aware deferral be combined to make clinical triage safer while maintaining useful coverage under temporal distribution shift?
methodology: The study uses the PhysioNet 2019 early-sepsis dataset with a temporally separated out-of-distribution test set and trains an MLP to predict sepsis six hours ahead. Probabilities are temperature-calibrated, and the authors compare vanilla split conformal prediction, gender-Mondrian conformal prediction, and importance-weighted conformal prediction. A single confidence-based deferral threshold is chosen on a held-out calibration set by minimizing an expected cost that weights false negatives, false positives, and deferrals differently, and the same threshold is then used on both in-distribution and temporally shifted data.

key_findings.finding: At 80% retained coverage, selective prediction reduced retained-case error by 49.6% on the in-distribution test set and 46.7% on the temporally shifted test set relative to predicting on every case.
The calibration-set cost optimization selected a deferral threshold of 0.8, yielding expected cost 0.5640 in distribution and 0.7053 under temporal shift, a 25.1% relative increase under shift.
Importance-weighted conformal prediction preserved target coverage better under temporal shift than the vanilla and gender-Mondrian variants, attaining 88.2% empirical coverage against a 90% target.
key_findings.section: Results: Conformal prediction under distribution shift

key_findings.finding: Temperature scaling produced low expected calibration error on both evaluations, with ECE 0.016 in distribution and 0.030 on the shifted test set.
Gender-Mondrian conformal prediction produced similar in-distribution coverage for female and male groups, with a reported coverage gap of 1.4 percentage points.

The clinical benefit of deferral depended materially on the assumed false-negative, false-positive, and deferral costs, and the originally optimized operating point was not uniformly superior to a trivial baseline under every evaluation condition.

limitations: The conformal guarantees rely on exchangeability, while the temporal out-of-distribution evaluation deliberately violates that assumption; empirical coverage consequently falls below the nominal level.
Importance-weighted conformal prediction requires access to representative unlabeled target covariates and depends on the quality of the estimated density ratio.
The study uses a single public sepsis dataset and therefore does not establish external validity across hospitals, clinical populations, modalities, or deployment workflows.
The deferral policy uses one offline calibration-selected threshold rather than an online mechanism that continually recalibrates under non-stationary streams.
Operational deferral can create clinician workload or treatment delay if escalation capacity is insufficient.
Cost-optimal conclusions are sensitive to the chosen cost vector, so the numerical operating point is not universally optimal.
The work evaluates patient-level predictive uncertainty rather than evidence completeness, compound claims, or longitudinal work-item state transitions.
raw_claims: The study formulates six-hour-ahead sepsis prediction as a selective clinical-triage problem.
The analytic cohort contains 2,155 patients with a reported sepsis prevalence of 7.0%.
A later-admission cohort is reserved as a temporal out-of-distribution test set.
The cost model assigns substantially greater cost to false negatives than to false positives.
The calibration procedure selects a confidence threshold of 0.8 for deferral.
Importance weighting gives the closest out-of-distribution coverage to the nominal conformal target among the evaluated conformal variants.
The same deferral threshold is applied without re-optimization to the in-distribution and temporally shifted test sets.
The authors make the implementation code public and use the publicly accessible PhysioNet 2019 challenge data.
